sections.name: body
sections.value:
# Role lifecycle boundaries and scoped actions

When reviewing retirement alongside queued sends, trace two separate flows: standing read through queued insertion, and queue preflight through writer commit and withdrawal. A sequential before/after test misses a send paused across either boundary. Ask for barrier-driven interleaving tests rather than another unprotected state read.

Git-first writes need a supported continuation when store work fails after the commit. An already-retired refusal must not prevent finishing explicitly authorized cleanup. Trace notification admission separately from deleting the source row; a successful transaction does not prove the subsequent FYI survives interruption.

Treat every suggested command as executable product output. Preserve project, role, instance and merge target; replay it from another project containing the same role. PR #126 already established the two-project invariant. Bare-role assignment does not drain a named-instance queue, and bare-role release does not match an instance holding.

Do not invent a hard one-holder invariant: existing assignment code warns on overlap rather than refusing it. Review against the repository's actual policy.

PR #135 at 3621220 supplied source counterexamples for these boundaries; CI's five sequential reshape tests passed. No local runtime reproduction was claimed. Exact-head JUnit verifies execution, but its log and artifact remain one CI origin.

magicWand: reuse a scoped directory-action constructor and replay its emitted commands in fixtures with two projects and named instances.

difficulties: lifecycle tests cover ordinary refusals but not admission interleavings or post-writer-commit recovery; shared reviewer LOG has multiple writers and no defined governance baton, so coordinate its append with the context owner.
